explainer.title: How the ATAR is put together
explainer.p1: Each course's HSC mark is the average of the school assessment mark and the exam mark. UAC scales each course, adds up the best 10 units (always including the best 2 units of English) and ranks every student in the state on that aggregate.
explainer.quoteDefault: A third of the points can still be close to the middle of the state.
explainer.quoteLive: {agg} points out of 500 is {pct}% of the marks — and roughly the {atar}th percentile of the state.
explainer.p2Rest: : the percentage of the Year 12 age group finished above. Marks scale down hard below each course's mean, so a modest share of the 500 points can still land mid-pack.

notes.title: Eligibility rules checked
notes.body: At least 10 ATAR units, including 2 units of English, at least three courses of 2 units or more, and at least four subjects. Since 2025 UAC no longer splits courses into Category A and B, so there's no longer a minimum of Category A units or a cap on Category B units.

notes.title: Scaling estimates
notes.body: Courses marked "estimated" use a generic scaling tier, not UAC data. They are there so every course produces a number, not so the number is exact. Courses added from the 2026 course list that the original calculator didn't cover use the generic average tier. Open "Course settings" on a subject to enter your own anchors.

notes.title: The ATAR curve
notes.body: A normal distribution fitted through two UAC reference points: aggregate 154.50 → ATAR 48.75 and aggregate 283.53 → ATAR 74.50. It is least accurate at the extremes.

notes.title: Moderation
notes.body: In the real HSC your assessment mark is replaced by the exam mark sitting at your rank in your school's cohort. The optional estimate places your rank on an assumed cohort distribution. It is a rough guide — the real result depends on how your classmates actually perform.

scaling.title: Every course and its scaling
scaling.intro: What each course's blended HSC mark becomes after scaling, out of 100 (halved for each unit). The small number is the change: marks lost to scaling are shown with a minus sign, marks gained with a plus. Courses on your list use your own settings.

sorts.up: Scales up most (at a mark of 70)
sorts.down: Scales down most (at a mark of 70)
sorts.name: Name

scaling.note: Every course uses a generic estimate tier, not UAC scaling data. Courses on your list use your own settings, including any anchors you enter. Course names, NESA numbers and unit values are from UAC's 2026 HSC course list.
